name: Clothing (onesies, pajamas, outerwear)
category_name: Infant and Child Durable Goods and Textiles (Ages 0-5)
anchor: Total-content children's-product and surface-coating law (US CPSIA s.101 and 16 CFR 1303; Canada SOR/2018-83 and SOR/2016-193; EU REACH Annex XVII entry 23; Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 coating values) for durable goods and fasteners, and the EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 extraction limits for clothing, bibs and bedding.
native_basis: extractable element content of the homogeneous textile material, determined after the extraction specified for REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 and expressed as mg/kg of the homogeneous material. This is an EXTRACTION basis. It is not a total-content basis (CPSIA substrate, Canadian surface-coating materials, REACH entry 23 cadmium, Australian coating content), and it is not the EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48/EC 0.07 M HCl toy-migration basis.
native_basis_label: extractable element content of the homogeneous textile material after the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 extraction (mg/kg of homogeneous material) — an extraction basis, not a total-content or toy-migration basis
scope_note: Bodysuits, onesies, sleepwear and pyjamas, everyday layers, outerwear, hats, mittens and socks for ages 0-5, including their prints, appliqués, linings, elastics and trims. Footwear is inside REACH Annex XVII entry 72's scope but is not a Category 10 taxonomy row and is not certified here. The metal snaps, zips and buttons attached to a garment are certified on the clasps-fasteners-infant-products row, on the total-content basis appropriate to a metal component, and are not homogenised into the textile extraction sample. Where the article incorporates a component that is itself a toy — a plush head or animal face on a comfort blanket, a sewn-on rattle or squeaker, a suspended teether ring, a crinkle or activity panel, or a soft book page — that component is separately in scope of Directive 2009/48/EC and must meet the EN 71-3 element-migration limits for its OWN material category. A textile or otherwise pliable toy component is Category I (dry, brittle, powder-like or pliable material); a moulded, coated or rigid toy component from which material can be scraped off is Category III. Those are 0.07 M HCl leachate limits measuring transfer out of the material, a different measured quantity from this row's after-extraction textile basis and from the total-content basis of the durable-goods rows, so they are recorded as a companion conformity obligation and are never published as this row's ceiling. Such a component is certified under Category 21 (Children's Toys, Arts, and Crafts) on the toy-migration basis appropriate to its material category, and is not homogenised into this row's textile extraction sample.
material: knitted and woven cotton, cotton-modal and cotton-polyester jersey, fleece and terry, with plastisol and water-based prints, elastane-containing ribbing, elastic waistbands, woven and printed labels and, on outerwear, coated or laminated shell fabric and polyester or down fill
components: base fabric of each colourway; rib, cuff and collar fabric; elastic and waistband; each print, plastisol transfer, appliqué and embroidery thread; lining and interlining; woven and printed label; outerwear shell coating or lamination and its fill — each homogeneous material sampled and extracted separately, per entry 72's homogeneous-material rule, with the darkest and most heavily printed colourway sampled first
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(migration|migratable|soluble|bioavailable|leachate|as consumed|as sold|edible|muscle meat|wet weight|product as placed on market))(?=.*after extraction)
basis_guard_note: Drawn at the boundary of the TEXTILE EXTRACTION family. The only register rows it admits are the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 limits, whose basis is 'homogeneous material after extraction'. It rejects total-content rows (CPSIA substrate, Canadian surface-coating materials, REACH entry 23 cadmium, Australian coating content), toy-migration rows (EN 71-3 0.07 M HCl), ASTM F963 soluble elements and EU 10/2011 specific migration into food. An extractable ceiling and a total-content ceiling are not interchangeable — a fabric can hold tens of mg/kg of total lead and release under 1 mg/kg on extraction — so the two are published separately and the content obligations are carried as disclosed companions.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable maximum set by a credible sovereign government for this exact product form in the row's declared native basis; a disclosed read-across from the nearest applicable sovereign cell where the exact cell is unregulated; a substantiated not-material determination where the analyte is a species bounded by a published parent; and a control with a named reference method where neither a sovereign value nor a supportable read-across exists. Never occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: extractable element content of the homogeneous textile material after the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 extraction (mg/kg of homogeneous material)
Pb.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12: 1 mg/kg lead in the homogeneous material after extraction.
Pb.substantiation: Entry 72 is the on-point sovereign instrument for infant and toddler clothing: its scope in the register is consumer clothing, related accessories, textiles with skin contact similar to clothing, and footwear, and its basis is the homogeneous material after extraction. At 1 mg/kg it is ninety times stricter than the 90 mg/kg total-content children's-product limits — but it is a DIFFERENT MEASURED QUANTITY, not a stricter version of the same one, and the two are not interchangeable. The total-content obligations therefore run alongside as companions and are enforced, not replaced: US CPSIA s.101 (100 mg/kg total lead in any part of a children's product), 16 CFR 1303 (90 mg/kg in a surface coating, which reaches a print or applied film on the garment), Canada SOR/2018-83 s.2(1) (90 mg/kg in each accessible part of child clothing and accessories) and Canada SOR/2016-193 s.2(1) and s.6 (90 mg/kg in a dried surface coating material and in applied stickers, films and coatings on products for children). A garment must satisfy both the extractable ceiling published here and the content companions. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value.

Cd.basis: extractable element content of the homogeneous textile material after the REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 extraction (mg/kg of homogeneous material)
Cd.label: EU REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12: 1 mg/kg cadmium in the homogeneous material after extraction.
Cd.substantiation: Entry 72 Appendix 12 binds infant and toddler clothing directly at 1 mg/kg extractable cadmium. The total-content companion obligations are EU REACH Annex XVII entry 23 (100 mg/kg cadmium in articles produced from the listed synthetic organic polymers, which reaches printed plastisol, laminated and coated panels and moulded trims) and the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 coating value (75 mg/kg on the non-volatile content of a coating material, which reaches a print or applied film). Both are enforced as companions in the content basis and neither is published here. Companion sub-national obligations, disclosed and not adopted as the anchor: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act (register rows wa_cspa2008_pb_childrens_products_90ppm, s.3(1)(a), and wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b)) prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component, and Minnesota Statutes 325E.3892 prohibits lead above 90 mg/kg and cadmium above 75 mg/kg in covered consumer products. Both are stricter than the adopted cadmium anchor. Neither is selected here because each statute's own product definition is narrower than the CPSIA 'children's product' definition and the register carries only the phrases 'children's products and product components covered by the Washington Children's Safe Product Act' and 'covered consumer products and product components listed in Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892, subject to exceptions', which do not establish whether this product form is inside the covered list. Applicability to the exact cell cannot be resolved from the register, so the rows are published as jurisdiction-specific companion obligations and logged as register gaps for scope-resolved re-ingest rather than selected as the HMTc value. COMPLIANCE OBLIGATION, in the content basis rather than this row's extraction basis: the Washington Children's Safe Product Act prohibits cadmium exceeding 40 mg/kg in a children's product or product component (register row wa_cspa2008_cd_childrens_products_40ppm, s.3(1)(b); codified in RCW chapter 70A.430), and its definition of a children's product expressly reaches products worn as clothing by children and products designed to help a child sleep. That 40 mg/kg is a TOTAL-CONTENT figure and is therefore not a stricter version of the 1 mg/kg extractable ceiling published here; the two measure different quantities and both bind. A component returning total cadmium above 40 mg/kg is escalated as a jurisdiction-specific regulatory hard stop under the HMTc legal-violation rule even where the extractable result conforms, pending scope-resolved re-ingest of the Washington row. Where the article incorporates a battery or a battery-powered module — a vibration unit, a sound or music module, a night light, a powered mobile or a powered rocker — the battery is a distinct regulated article with its own instrument, and its limits are not this row's. Regulation (EU) 2023/1542 restricts cadmium in a portable battery whether or not incorporated into an appliance (register row eu_batteries_2023_cd_portable_batteries_20000, 20 mg/kg) and mercury in a battery (register row eu_batteries_2023_thg_batteries_5000, 5 mg/kg), both expressed on the weight of the battery. Both are stricter than the values published here and both are recorded as companion obligations on the battery in a battery-by-weight basis; the battery is never homogenised into an accessible-component sample and its instrument is never merged into this row's extractable ceiling. Where the article carries no battery and no powered module the obligation does not arise.

tAs.substantiation: Entry 72 Appendix 12 limits arsenic compounds expressed as As metal at 1 mg/kg after extraction; the register maps the row to total arsenic and records explicitly that it is not an inorganic-arsenic value. It is therefore published on the tAs cell and never on iAs. The Australian coating-content arsenic value (25 mg/kg) is a companion in the content basis for any print or applied film on the garment.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic limit for a textile. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12, the instrument that governs this row, limits arsenic compounds expressed as As metal — a total-element value, as the register records — and every other arsenic instrument that reaches a children's article is likewise unspeciated. Inorganic arsenic is a proper subset of total arsenic by identity, so the published 1 mg/kg extractable total-arsenic ceiling on this same row bounds it absolutely and a separate inorganic ceiling would add no protection. Arsenic in infant and toddler clothing arises as residual arsenic in dyestuff, pigment and mordant feedstocks rather than through a separate organoarsenical route, so the total ceiling is not evaded by speciation. Arsenic-based dyestuffs are obsolete in every jurisdiction checked and no residual arsenical finishing chemistry is in commercial use for infant apparel.
iAs.reference_method: Total-arsenic determination on the entry 72 Appendix 12 extract by ICP-MS, with reflex inorganic-arsenic speciation by HPLC-ICP-MS reserved for any homogeneous material whose extractable total arsenic exceeds half the published ceiling. No routine speciation is required while the total sits below that trigger.
iAs.substantiation: Bounded by a published sovereign number in the row's own native basis, so this is a speciation bound against a real ceiling rather than an assertion that arsenic is absent.
iAs.regulatory_basis: REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 (arsenic compounds, 1 mg/kg after extraction, expressed as As metal) is published on this row's tAs cell as a firm sovereign ceiling in the row's own native basis; no jurisdiction publishes an inorganic-arsenic value for clothing, related accessories, textiles in clothing-like skin contact, or footwear.
iAs.jurisdictions_checked: EU (REACH Annex XVII entries 23, 27, 47, 72; Directive 2009/48/EC), US (CPSIA s.101, 16 CFR 1303, ASTM F963 via CPSIA s.106), Canada (SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-83), Australia (Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2), UK, Codex — register-checked, no inorganic-arsenic row for any textile or article scope.

tHg.rationale: REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 sets no mercury value, so this row's native extraction basis carries no sovereign mercury ceiling, and no credible sovereign publishes an extractable-mercury maximum for infant and toddler clothing. The mercury instruments that do reach the article are content-basis limits on a print, coating or applied film — Canada SOR/2016-193 s.5, 10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material, and s.6's companion scope for applied stickers, films and coatings on products for children. Publishing a content number as this row's extractable ceiling would conflate two measured quantities, so it is carried as a companion obligation instead and no extractable number is invented.
tHg.reference_method: Mandatory total-mercury content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion with CV-AFS or ICP-MS on the base textile and, separately, on every print, plastisol transfer, coating, applied film, appliqué and trim, dispositioned against the 10 mg/kg Canadian surface-coating-material companion criterion for the coated components. Any detection above the reporting limit in the base textile triggers dyehouse and finishing-chemistry review and supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury is a marine-bioaccumulation species. It has no formation route and no established industrial source in infant and toddler clothing: the mercury that can occur here comes from pigment, catalyst and preservative residues in coatings, polymers and dyestuffs, all of which are inorganic or aryl-mercury chemistries, and organomercury fungicides in these materials have been withdrawn across every jurisdiction checked. Every sovereign mercury instrument that reaches this article class is written on TOTAL mercury; not one sets a methylmercury value for an article, a coating or a textile. Methylmercury is a proper subset of total mercury by identity, so the mandatory total-mercury control on this row, together with the 10 mg/kg Canadian surface-coating-material companion ceiling that binds any print or applied film, bounds it absolutely and a separate methylmercury ceiling would add no protection.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury content screen by microwave-assisted acid digestion with CV-AFS or ICP-MS on every accessible component, with reflex methylmercury speciation by GC-ICP-MS reserved for any component that both exceeds the total-mercury reporting limit and carries a declared organomercury input. No routine methylmercury determination is required.
MeHg.substantiation: Classified no-migration-pathway rather than speciation-bounded because this row publishes no total-mercury number in its native basis: REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 sets no mercury value, so the total-mercury parent is a mandatory control rather than a published ceiling and a speciation bound would have no published parent to bind against. The determination rests on the material argument instead — no organomercury input and no formation route in a finished textile — with the total-mercury control and the 10 mg/kg Canadian surface-coating-material companion criterion bounding any print or applied film.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for an article, a surface coating or a textile. The mercury instruments that reach this category are Canada SOR/2016-193 s.5 (10 mg/kg total mercury in a dried sample of surface coating material), Canada SOR/2011-17 s.23(1)(c) (10 mg/kg total mercury in accessible toy coatings), the Australian Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2 toy-coating value (60 mg/kg, unspeciated) and Directive 2009/48/EC Annex II Part III (total-mercury migration) — all total-element.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU (REACH Annex XVII entries 23, 27, 47, 63, 72; Directive 2009/48/EC; Directive 2011/65/EU RoHS; Regulation 10/2011), US (CPSIA s.101, 16 CFR 1303, ASTM F963 via CPSIA s.106), Canada (SOR/2016-193, SOR/2018-82, SOR/2018-83, SOR/2011-17), Australia (Customs (Prohibited Imports) Regulations 1956 Schedule 2), UK, Codex — register-checked, no methylmercury row for any article, coating or textile scope.

Ni.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a nickel CONTENT maximum for infant and toddler clothing. The governing instrument for the actual hazard — allergic contact dermatitis from prolonged skin contact with metal snaps, zip sliders and teeth, rivets, eyelets and decorative metal trim attached to the garment — is the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 nickel-release restriction, which is expressed as an areal release rate (µg/cm² per week) and therefore cannot be expressed in this register's µg/kg content unit; it is not present in the register in any form. The EN 71-3 toy nickel migration values and the EU 10/2011 nickel specific-migration value both sit in leachate bases outside this row's native basis. No number is invented: the cell is held under mandatory analytical control.
Ni.reference_method: Mandatory total-nickel content analysis of every accessible metal, plated and alloy component by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, plus EN 1811 nickel-release testing (with EN 12472 wear-and-corrosion pre-treatment for coated or plated parts) on every component in prolonged skin contact, dispositioned against the release criterion in the REACH Annex XVII entry 27 restriction as a companion conformity obligation. That criterion's numeric value is deliberately NOT reproduced here: the restriction is absent from data/evidence/regulatory_limits.csv, and this standard quotes no number that is not carried by a named register row. The criterion is applied from the instrument text at audit and is logged as a register gap for ingest through the verified regulatory-fetch pathway. Any component exceeding the release criterion, or any total-nickel result that is an outlier against the supplier's own qualification data, triggers supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule.

Sn.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a tin value for infant and toddler clothing in this row's extraction basis, and none publishes a total-tin content maximum for it either. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12, the instrument this row is built on, lists lead, cadmium, arsenic and chromium(VI) and does not list tin, so the row's own native basis carries no tin number at all. The instrument that does reach this article class — REACH Annex XVII entry 20, which covers textile articles intended to come into contact with the skin, childcare articles and other consumer articles in skin contact — restricts ORGANOTIN (dibutyltin and dioctyltin) expressed as tin at 0.1 % by weight, that is 1 000 mg/kg (register row eu_reach_entry20_dot_skin_contact_articles_0_1pct). Adopting that number here would cross two boundaries at once. Organotin expressed as tin is a different MEASURAND from total tin, so publishing it as this row's total-tin ceiling would pass a speciated restriction off as a total-element limit; and 0.1 % by weight is a total-content figure, so publishing it here would additionally pass a content restriction off as an extractable one. An analyte boundary is never crossed, with or without disclosure, and that is the whole reason no number is published on this cell. The organotin restriction is carried as a companion obligation instead and no total-tin number is invented. This is not a double standard against the chromium cells on the same row, and the contrast is worth stating precisely: hexavalent chromium is published here as a DIRECT sovereign value because entry 72 Appendix 12 writes a chromium(VI) number in this row's own extraction basis (register row eu_2018_1513_cr_vi_consumer_textiles_1mgkg, 1 mg/kg), while the REACH Annex XVII entry 47 leather limit for that same species (register row eu_301_2014_cr_vi_leather_articles_3mgkg, 3 mg/kg on the total dry weight of leather) runs alongside as a content companion and is never merged into the extractable ceiling. Chromium has a value in this row's basis; tin has none, in this basis or in the content basis, for the correct analyte. That is the difference, and it is a difference in what the instruments say rather than in what is convenient.
Sn.reference_method: Mandatory total-tin content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS, with reflex organotin speciation by GC-ICP-MS (dibutyltin, dioctyltin, tributyltin, triphenyltin) on any component returning total tin above the reporting limit. Speciated results are dispositioned against the REACH Annex XVII entry 20 0.1 %-as-tin companion criterion; total-tin results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule against the tightest available supplier qualification context.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes an aluminium limit for infant and toddler clothing in any basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 does not list aluminium, and the EN 71-3 and EU 10/2011 aluminium values are leachate limits for toys and food-contact plastics. Aluminium is additionally a deliberate input here — aluminium salts serve as mordants, as flame-retardant and water-repellent finish components, and as the substrate of aluminium-lake pigments — so a contamination ceiling on total aluminium would not distinguish specification from contamination. No number is invented.
Al.reference_method: Mandatory total-aluminium content analysis by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the base textile and on each print, coating and finish, with declared mordant, finish and pigment inputs recorded on the technical file. Aluminium found in a component whose declared chemistry contains no aluminium input is treated as a contamination signal and escalated to supplier corrective action under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign publishes a TOTAL-chromium value for infant and toddler clothing in this row's extraction basis. REACH Annex XVII entry 72 Appendix 12 regulates chromium(VI) specifically and not total chromium, which is the correct regulatory choice: total chromium in a textile is dominated by benign trivalent chromium from chrome-tanned leather trim, chromium(III) mordants and chromium-complex dyes, while the health-relevant species is Cr(VI), and that species carries a firm published 1 mg/kg extractable ceiling on this same row. The Australian coating-content value (60 mg/kg) and the ASTM F963 soluble value (60 mg/kg) sit in other bases. Publishing a total-chromium ceiling would add no protection over the published Cr(VI) ceiling and would misrepresent a benign total as a hazard measure, so total chromium is held as a screening control.
Cr.reference_method: Mandatory total-chromium content screen by microwave-assisted acid digestion and ICP-MS on the base textile, on each dyed and printed component and on any leather or chrome-tanned trim. A total-chromium detection is the trigger for the Cr(VI) determination published on this same row; total chromium itself carries no ceiling and is dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule against the supplier's own dye and tanning specification.
